title: Transit Gateway (hub-and-spoke)
hook: AWS Transit Gateway (TGW) is a Regional hub that connects Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs), Site-to-Site VPN, and Direct Connect gateways in a hub-and-spoke model. Unlike VPC peering, routing through TGW can be transitive when you design route tables deliberately.

blocks.text: Transit Gateway is a managed Layer 3 router in your Region. Attachments include VPCs, VPN connections, Direct Connect gateways, and peering to other TGWs. Each attachment associates with a TGW route table that controls which CIDR blocks are reachable — enabling shared-services spokes without full mesh among app VPCs.

entries.plainDefinition: Connection between TGW and a VPC, VPN, or Direct Connect gateway.
Hub routing domain deciding forwarding between attachments.
Automatically adds attachment CIDRs into a TGW route table.
Binds an attachment to exactly one TGW route table for forwarding decisions.
entries.example: Prod VPC attachment associated with prod RT only.

blocks.text: Enterprises outgrow N-squared VPC peering. Hybrid designs centralize on-prem paths on one TGW instead of a Virtual Private Gateway per VPC. Interviewers test route domain segmentation, blackhole routes, and when inter-Region TGW peering is worth the complexity.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: TGW is transitive only within the route tables you design — association plus propagation or static routes, not automatic full mesh.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Create TGW
items.body: Regional hub; disable default association/propagation for strict designs.

items.title: Attach VPC spokes
items.body: Dedicated subnets per AZ for TGW ENIs; add VPC routes sending remote CIDRs to TGW.

items.title: Configure TGW route tables
items.body: Associate attachments; propagate or add static routes for allowed paths.

items.title: Attach hybrid
items.body: Site-to-Site VPN or Direct Connect gateway shares on-prem prefixes to selected RTs.

snippet.label: CLI — create TGW and VPC attachment
snippet.code:
aws ec2 create-transit-gateway \
  --description prod-hub \
  --options DefaultRouteTableAssociation=disable,DefaultRouteTablePropagation=disable

aws ec2 create-transit-gateway-vpc-attachment \
  --transit-gateway-id tgw-0abc123 \
  --vpc-id vpc-prod \
  --subnet-ids subnet-tgw-a subnet-tgw-b
snippet.explanation: Disabling defaults forces explicit RT design. TGW ENIs consume IPs in attachment subnets — plan /28 per AZ.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — TGW route table association
snippet.code:
HubTgw:
  Type: AWS::EC2::TransitGateway
  Properties:
    Description: prod-hub

ProdRouteTable:
  Type: AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayRouteTable
  Properties:
    TransitGatewayId: !Ref HubTgw

ProdAssociation:
  Type: AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayRouteTableAssociation
  Properties:
    TransitGatewayAttachmentId: !Ref ProdVpcAttachment
    TransitGatewayRouteTableId: !Ref ProdRouteTable
snippet.explanation: Association picks the routing domain. Add AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayRouteTablePropagation or static routes separately.

snippet.label: CLI — static route to shared services
snippet.explanation: Static routes when propagation is off — prod spokes reach shared CIDR only, not each other.

snippet.label: CLI — debug route lookup
snippet.explanation: Finds which attachment owns the route for a destination — first step for hybrid blackholes.

blocks.title: Network vs application routing
rows: HTTP/gRPC routes are URLs, not VPC CIDRs
502 from ALB when target SG blocks TGW-sourced traffic

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Missing VPC route table entry pointing remote CIDR to TGW. One TGW RT with all attachments propagated — dev reaches prod. Undersized TGW attachment subnets.

blocks.text: TGW charges hourly per attachment plus data processing. Blackhole routes appear when static routes reference deleted attachments. Inter-Region TGW peering adds cross-Region data charges. How to prove it in production: search-transit-gateway-routes during incidents; VPC Flow Logs show packets to TGW ENI; CloudWatch metrics on PacketDropCountBlackhole when enabled.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Not transitive; ops nightmare at scale

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying TGW automatically connects every attached VPC. Strong answer: association binds an attachment to one RT; propagation/static routes define who can reach which CIDRs.

interviewTakeaways: Transit Gateway enables transitive routing through route tables — unlike pairwise VPC peering.
Association plus propagation (or static routes) defines reachability — not attachment alone.
Place TGW attachment subnets in every AZ; VPC route tables must send remote CIDR to TGW.
60s: Regional L3 hub. Attach VPC, VPN, DX. Segment with TGW route tables. Replace peering mesh. Debug with search-transit-gateway-routes and Flow Logs.
Follow-up: how do you attach on-prem prefixes to only prod, not staging, on one TGW?
commonPitfalls: Assuming all TGW attachments talk to each other — that gets you rejected; route tables must explicitly allow paths.
Strong answer: name association, propagation, and static routes as the three levers.
Forgetting VPC-side routes to TGW for inter-spoke traffic.
Single route table propagated with every attachment — blast radius spans environments.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node services call ALB hostnames resolved by Route53 private zones. TGW forwards IP packets only — SG rules on targets must allow TGW-sourced traffic.
A TypeScript backend-for-frontend calling APIs in three VPCs still needs TGW routes and SG rules per hop — types do not replace network design.
